verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew safely returned to Earth on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The Artemis II crew is officially home after their Orion spacecraft splashed down as planned... on April 10, 2026." (R1); "SPLASHDOWN! ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT" (R2, implying April 10); "April 10, 2026... splashed down" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm safe splashdown and return on April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashed down ... in the Pacific Ocean off San Diego" (R1); "splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego" (R2); "splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state the location as Pacific Ocean off San Diego/California coast.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "landed ... at 8:07 p.m. ET" (R1); "at 8:07 p.m. EDT" (R2); "at 8:07 p.m. EDT" (R3); "00:07 - Splashdown" (R5, corresponding to 8:07 p.m. EDT); "at 8:07 p.m. ET" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm exact time of 8:07 p.m. EDT/ET.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Commander Reid Wiseman, mission pilot Victor Glover, and mission specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen" (R1); "NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and ... Jeremy Hansen" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: All sources list exactly these four crew members.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew completed a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "historic 10-day Artemis II mission" (R1); "approximate 10-day mission" (R2); "historic 10-day mission" (R3); "nearly 10-day journey" (R4); "10-day journey" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as a 10-day mission across sources, despite precise elapsed time slightly under 10 days.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission broke the record for the farthest distance humans have ever traveled into space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "farther from Earth than any humans had gone before, beating the previous record set by Apollo 13" (R1); "farthest than any humans have ever traveled before, surpassing ... Apollo 13" (R4); "travelled further from Earth than anyone before them" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state it broke the distance record previously held by Apollo 13.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is safe and in good health.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "all four crew members are safe and well" (R1); "safely aboard" (R2); "'hale and hearty'" (R3); "safely back" (R4); "happy and healthy" (R5); "Four green crewmembers ... in good shape" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm crew safety and good health post-splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew successfully splashed down at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "successfully ... at 8:07 p.m. ET" (R1); "successfully completed a parachute-assisted splashdown ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT" (R2); "flawless splashdown ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm successful splashdown at the exact time.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew was retrieved from the Orion capsule by the recovery team on the USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "hoisted ... to the USS John P. Murtha for medical exams" (R1); "safely aboard the USS John P. Murtha" (R2); "now on the USS John P. Murtha" (R3); "transported them via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources detail recovery from capsule and transport to USS John P. Murtha by recovery teams.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission tested the spacecraft's systems in preparation for future lunar landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "analysis of how the Orion spacecraft performed will likely begin soon in order to prepare for Artemis III and Artemis IV missions" (R1); "post-flight checks" (R2); "put Orion through a full in‑flight evaluation ... for future missions to the Moon" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe it as a test mission evaluating systems for future Artemis lunar landings.

verifications.claim: According to NBC News, the Artemis II astronauts completed their mission successfully.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No reference is from or attributes information to NBC News; success is reported but not sourced to NBC.
